The cleavable assay uses a 1000-fold excess of ribozyme over labelled substrate and a stem III shortened to 5 bp. It is a single-turnover progress experiment, not a measured multiple-turnover kcat or persistence through repeated cycles.

The source specifies 100 micromolar MgCl2 plus 500 mM NaCl at pH 7.0 and 25 C; the high sodium concentration is part of the preparation. A statement of activity at low magnesium alone must not omit this 500 mM sodium background or call the complete solution physiological.

The source does not print absolute RNA concentrations for this assay in the reviewed Methods. The reported 0.05 min^-1 comes from a fitted gel progress curve with no supplied error estimate here; no new fit or zero-rate bound for the control is calculated.

The loop-removal catalytic control differs from the more extensively altered FRET control. Virtually no detectable cleavage over 30 min is a finite assay observation, not an exactlyzero microscopic rate or universal requirement for those loops.

Site-specific cleavage and its absence/reduction in a sequence variant support finite RNA functionality; no broad substrate-specificity panel, equilibrium binding constant, regulation or RNA-only metabolism is measured.

records.name: Prepared noncleavable hammerhead I-III FRET titration
openObligations: The FRET construct contains a 2-prime-deoxy-C17 to prevent cleavage and dye labels near stems I and III. The catalytic assay restores ribo-C17, removes dyes, shortens stem III and changes salt/temperature conditions. No unqualified matched conformation-to-chemistry rate law is admitted.

Penedo FRET spectra are steady-state measurements at 4 C; titration steps vary ion concentration, not elapsed folding time. The source one-step/two-step language describes fitted transitions across concentration and does not measure temporal folding rate constants.
The fluorophore pair reports relative dye geometry. For this I-III vector, magnesium addition lowers FRET as these arms separate. Higher FRET is not a universal marker of folded or active RNA.

The disrupted FRET construct removes the stem I internal loop, lengthens stem II by 3 bp and replaces its terminal loop; the response cannot isolate the energy of one tertiary contact from all accompanying changes.

The source gives RNA construction/annealing in 90 mM Tris-borate pH 8.3 but does not print a separate complete FRET measurement-buffer/RNA-concentration prescription in the reviewed Methods. Do not silently use construction buffer as a fully specified measurement solution.
The fitted 160 micromolar midpoint and n 0.85 have no supplied confidence intervals in this report. R0.998 is a fit-correlation statistic, not parameter uncertainty or independent replication.

openObligations: Photon absorption, a successful isomerization and a later electrical or biochemical response are different events. The reviewed Kim yield is below unity and wavelength dependent; no deterministic conversion of every absorbed photon or universal quantum yield is admitted.

The Gruhl preparation is purified bovine rhodopsin crystals under a room-temperature laser pump and serial X-ray readout. Multiphoton influence cannot be excluded. Its early structural intermediate cannot be relabeled as a verified native isolated-single-photon trajectory or the later G-protein-binding state.

Peteanu is retained at abstract-and-bibliographic-metadata reading, Kim at abstract-and-figure-caption reading, and Gruhl at its existing selected-full-text reading. No additional passages, mutation experiments, raw spectra, structural refinement or yield fit have been reviewed or replayed by this reuse audit. Species unresolved by the two abstracts remain unresolved.

The sources supply study-scoped spectral conversion, source-reported early structural changes and a separate wavelength-dependent yield. They do not identify each individual chemical occurrence, derive a universal quantization rule, or provide a shared excitation/response model across their different preparations.

An already prepared protein/chromophore is an assay input. The protein-folding scope is not a folding event measured in these assays, a developmental history of the pigment or a demonstrated necessary formation mechanism.

Quantum effects in chemical reactions are now scoped to cryogenic matrix-isolated ground-singlet H-C-OH dark loss and a distinct reduced reaction-path/WKB interpretation. That experiment/model cannot establish rhodopsin excited-state dynamics, photoisomerization pathways or a necessary tunnelling mechanism.

Molecular resonance is now scoped to a stationary six-electron benzene valence-bond model and its reference-defined energy lowering. It supplies no retinal absorption spectrum, excited-state path, dynamic hopping among resonance drawings or quantitative rhodopsin delocalization mediator.

Generic transition-state stabilization supplies no matched calculation or intervention for this photochemical pathway. A thermal enzyme-barrier description cannot substitute for a specified excited-state pigment model or make the biochemical photoproduct an enzyme-catalytic turnover.

Generic hydration and ionic-microenvironment descriptions supply no measured hydration-mediated effect in these selected pigment assays. Protein/solvent context does not by itself identify a causal solvent mediator, quantitative energy transfer or measured necessity.

Early photochemistry can be placed beside existing rod-current and transducin/PDE observations only as a preparation-aware literature interpretation. The current separate assays do not provide an end-to-end matched cascade, universal amplification factor, regulation/integration mechanism, electrical sufficiency, spike response or sensory/neural outcome.
